what: Static analysis of the vault's contracts (the approved release's, unmodified) with Slither
tool: Slither 0.11.6, solc 0.8.26 through SOLC_VERSION, Foundry build with via_ir as the release configures it
how: A copy of chain/vendor/{foundry.toml,contracts,lib} was made in a scratch directory and analysed there; the workspace copy and the approved release were not touched. Command: slither . --filter-paths "lib/|contracts/test/|contracts/script/" --exclude-informational --exclude-optimization

triage.judgement: Not exploitable as flagged. The line before the transfer reverts unless the caller is the obligation's debtor, and only a debtor can create an obligation for itself (issue uses msg.sender). The function is nonReentrant and clears the obligation before the transfer.

Not exploitable as flagged. trade is nonReentrant. The values called stale are balance differences recomputed after the external calls, which is the intended accounting: only what this trade moved is counted. It does rely on the venues being the pools the owner named.
Benign: a guard against a zero-output hop, and a test pool's input check.
Benign. The ignored values are a pool's timestamp, a bound, an id, and a signature-recovery error code whose failure case (zero signer) is rejected explicitly on the next line.
Benign. Ownership transfer is two-step, so a zero address can never accept. The verifier rejects a zero signer whatever the configured vendor is.
The five read are accumulators that rely on Solidity's zero initialisation. The other eleven were not read.
Not read one by one. Validity windows and due dates compare with the block time by design.
Not read one by one. Loops over hops and venues, which the contracts bound by constants.
An event emitted after an external call; ordering of logs only.

conclusion: No finding was judged exploitable. All three high-severity findings and the security-relevant medium and low ones were read against the code. This is one tool and one reader, on contracts that are not QED workspace code: it is not an audit. An independent audit is a requirement before any real funds.
